% tagged-table — a table whose grid the structure tree declares.
%
% One concern: does a declared cell reach the output in its own row and column? The
% 788 tagged tables in the corpus are asserted only by counts — a section total, a block
% floor — and a count cannot tell a correct grid from a transposed one, nor a header row
% from a promoted data row. This is the byte-exact yardstick for the path that reads
% Table/TR/TD/TH, and table.pdf is not it: that file is untagged, so it exercises the
% geometry the layout reader has no grid logic for and says nothing about this path.
%
% The defect it was written for emitted every one of those 788 tables as scattered
% paragraphs. Of 17482 TD and TH elements on disk, 0 hold marked content of their own —
% all of them wrap their text in a P — and sectionize detached that P, so the cell had no
% spans, IsEmpty dropped it, and the text reappeared outside the table it belonged to.
% That is the LI > LBody > P defect tagged-lists.tex was written for, one element name
% over, which is why both fixtures exist rather than one: they fail independently, and a
% single gold file asserting lists and tables together reads the same either way.
%
% Header cells in the first row, because the header row is the one decision GFM forces
% that the tree does not make for us. 773 of the corpus's 788 tables declare an all-TH
% first row and 11 declare no header there at all, and the sink treats those differently —
% an empty header row rather than a promoted data row, since promoting one relabels data
% as a column name. Only the declared case is committed here; the other is a constructed
% unit fixture, because no producer on disk emits a headerless table and LaTeX will not
% write one.
%
% Three columns and three body rows. Two of either cannot distinguish a transposed read
% from a correct one, and the corpus's own column counts cluster at 3 (628 of 788).
% Deliberately absent: spans, nesting, and a row-header column. All three are on disk —
% 69 ColSpan, 43 RowSpan, 13 nested, 598 with a TH below row 0 — and none is expressible
% in GFM, so a fixture asserting them would be asserting the workaround rather than the
% behaviour. They are recorded in doc.Cell and in DESIGN.md §10 instead.
%
% Build with lualatex, not pdflatex, for the reason clauses.tex records at length:
% pdfTeX's tagging backend writes /MCID 1 into every /MCR while the content stream draws
% an increasing sequence, so all but one structure element joins to nothing. The committed
% PDF means a clone never builds either.
%
% tagging-setup=table/header-rows is required and is not the default: a plain tabular
% under tagging=on declares every cell a TD, which is the headerless shape, and the first
% build of this fixture did exactly that. The key needs the testphase table module, which
% is what turns row 1's cells into TH — the shape 773 of the corpus's 788 tables have and
% the one GFM's header row expresses.
\DocumentMetadata{pdfstandard=ua-2, tagging=on,
  tagging-setup={table/header-rows={1}}}
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage{latex-lab-testphase-table}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}

\begin{tabular}{lll}
Header A & Header B & Header C \\
Cell A1 & Cell B1 & Cell C1 \\
Cell A2 & Cell B2 & Cell C2 \\
\end{tabular}

\end{document}
